- Pipeline (L301-305): canonicalise and scrub, prefilter on exact handles and facets, FTS5 BM25 rank (three tables), abstain on score-free features. Coverage = IDF-weighted share of query terms matched; margin = coverage gap to second place. Lead needs strong exact hit AND coverage >= theta_lead AND margin >= mu AND validated status AND no unmet precondition. Candidate needs coverage >= theta_cand or any exact handle. Everything else is a miss. Shown: at most one lead and one candidate, 2,000-char cap.
- Scope of what is cached: diagnosis path, negative results, fix, check. Not whole solves. In Opus-reserved areas "the store has saved the diagnosis, not the whole solve" (L444, L690).

findings.text: [narrowed] B10 (DECIDE, light): Two settings off; turn on Docker sign-in autostart and unless-stopped on two DBs; self-starting preflight; resume list. EVIDENCE: compose.yaml has no 'restart' key (grep today, empty). machine-facts: AutoStart false. The problem recurred on the last day: 'a first run failed only because Docker Desktop was not running' (clinic-build/task.md:821, 11 Nov). Cross-effects: an automatic restart plus resume of every slice at sign-in is the pattern that produced the 2030 s queue wait on 9 Nov. If B05 turns out thermal or PSU, auto-restarting all load at boot invites a repeat. AMENDMENT: Add staggered resume (at most two slices) and keep auto-restart scoped to two DBs until B05 is diagnosed.

findings.text: [stands] B06 (DECIDE, none): Container mode is the measured faster gate; native becomes a path-triggered canary; serial pass in its own lane as a trial. EVIDENCE: linux-test-runner/task.md:212-218: container runs 318.8-360.1 s against native 475.5 s on a loaded day. The hinted blocker does not apply: the two Linux-only failures were fixed in the tests (task.md:258, 261: 'the only two tests of the 2,472 that fail on Linux ... fixed', 19b3906). Two side effects are unstated. The container runs 12 workers against native's 6, and order-dependent tests have already bitten twice: S02 V1 'pass only because files run alphabetically' (sweep-tables), and on 11 Nov 2 of 2570 failed order-dependently (clinic-build/task.md:821). Running the serial lane beside the parallel pass also adds a second database and raises peak memory (B07, B08). AMENDMENT: Add: expect one fix-up round for order-dependent tests when the worker count changes. Measure peak memory in the serial-lane trial before counting its time gain.
